NOTICE OF EXEMPT OFFERING OF SECURITIES

Narrative Supplement to Form D

Issuer: Calderbrook Bioscience, Inc.
CIK: 0002041877
Jurisdiction of Incorporation: Delaware
Principal Place of Business: 1180 Trapelo Road, Waltham, Massachusetts 02451
Date of First Sale: July 14, 2026

1. THE ISSUER

Calderbrook Bioscience, Inc. is a corporation organized under the laws of the State of Delaware, with its principal place of business in Waltham, Massachusetts. The Issuer develops enzyme-replacement therapies for lysosomal storage disorders. The Issuer's Form D was filed on EDGAR under CIK 0002041877 within fifteen (15) days after the date of first sale.

2. EXEMPTION CLAIMED

The offering described in this narrative is made in reliance on the exemption from registration provided by Section 4(a)(2) of the Securities Act of 1933 and Rule 506(b) of Regulation D promulgated under that Act. The securities have not been registered under the Securities Act or under the securities laws of any state, and may not be offered or resold absent registration or an available exemption.

The Issuer elected Rule 506(b) rather than Rule 506(c) because the Issuer does not intend to engage in general solicitation and does not wish to undertake the verification obligations Rule 506(c) imposes.

3. PURCHASERS AND ACCREDITED-INVESTOR REPRESENTATIONS

All purchasers in the offering are accredited investors as that term is defined in Rule 501(a) of Regulation D. No securities were sold to any non-accredited investor. Each purchaser executed a subscription agreement containing a written representation of the purchaser's accredited investor status, the category of accreditation relied on, a representation that the purchaser is acquiring the securities for investment and not with a view to distribution, and an acknowledgment of the restricted nature of the securities.

Because the offering is made under Rule 506(b), the Issuer is not required to take reasonable steps to verify accredited investor status, and it has not done so. The Issuer relied on the purchasers' written representations, on its pre-existing substantive relationship with each purchaser, and on the completed investor questionnaires collected before any offer was made. Had the Issuer relied on Rule 506(c), it would have been required to verify each purchaser's status through the methods listed in Rule 506(c)(2)(ii).

4. GENERAL SOLICITATION

The Issuer did not engage in general solicitation or general advertising in connection with the offering. No offer was made through any public web page, press release, seminar, social media post, mailing to persons with whom the Issuer had no pre-existing relationship, or any other form of general advertising. Rule 506(b) prohibits general solicitation, and the Issuer's officers and placement agent were instructed in writing that any such communication would forfeit the exemption. Each offeree had a substantive pre-existing relationship with the Issuer or with its placement agent established before the offering commenced.

5. BAD-ACTOR DISQUALIFICATION

The Issuer conducted a bad-actor inquiry under Rule 506(d) covering each covered person: the Issuer, its predecessors, its directors, its executive officers and other officers participating in the offering, its 20% beneficial owners, the placement agent and its principals, and each promoter connected with the Issuer. Each covered person completed a written questionnaire addressing every disqualifying event enumerated in Rule 506(d)(1), and the Issuer obtained a certification from each. No covered person is subject to a disqualifying event. Had a disqualifying event occurred before September 23, 2013, the Issuer would have made the disclosure Rule 506(e) requires.

6. OFFERING AMOUNT AND MINIMUM INVESTMENT

The aggregate offering amount is $24,000,000 of Series B Preferred Stock. The minimum investment is $250,000, which the Issuer may waive in its discretion for an existing stockholder. As of the date of this narrative, $18,750,000 has been sold to eleven purchasers, and $5,250,000 remains available. There is no minimum aggregate offering amount that must be raised before the Issuer may accept subscriptions, and subscription funds are not held in escrow.

7. STATE BLUE-SKY NOTICE FILINGS

Rule 506 offerings are covered securities under Section 18(b)(4)(F) of the Securities Act and NSMIA, so state registration is preempted. The Issuer will nonetheless make a state notice filing, and pay the applicable fee, in each state in which a purchaser resides, within the period each state's blue-sky statute requires — generally fifteen (15) days after the first sale in that state. The Issuer has made notice filings in Massachusetts, New York, California, Texas, and Illinois.

8. USE OF PROCEEDS AND SALES COMPENSATION

The Issuer will use the proceeds for clinical development of its lead program, for working capital, and for general corporate purposes. Bellhaven Securities LLC, a broker-dealer registered under Section 15 of the Exchange Act and a member of FINRA, acted as placement agent and received a cash commission of 6% of the gross proceeds. No finder's fee was paid to any person not registered as a broker-dealer.

This narrative supplements the Issuer's Form D and does not constitute an offer to sell or a solicitation of an offer to buy any security.
